 Published On Nov 15, 2026 | 05:00 IST 
 Last Updated On Nov 15, 2026 | 05:00 IST

 PTI AI Summary A deepening low-pressure system over the southern waters is gathering force to trigger widespread heavy downpours, severe gale winds, and extremely rough seas across eastern coastal belts and island territories. Fishermen face total bans as authorities track its impending landfall trajectory.
 + Follow on Google Add as preferred source A low-pressure area over the Southeast Bay of Bengal may intensify into a cyclonic storm by November 16, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast. The weather agency has also predicted rainfall over Andaman & Nicobar Islands till November 18.
 Scattered showers are likely over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam and Meghalaya from November 15 to 17.
 Cyclonic storm possible over Bay of Bengal 
 The weather system in the Bay of Bengal shifted into a Well-Marked Low-Pressure Area on Saturday morning. The system is likely to move north-northwestwards and intensify into a cyclonic storm over the central Bay of Bengal around the evening of November 16. If the storm reaches the required cyclonic conditions, it will be named as Cyclone Akvan. 
 Rainfall predicted around Bay of Bengal, Northeast 
 Isolated heavy rainfall is likely over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands till November 16. There is a possibility of fairly widespread to widespread rainfall over the region till November 18.
 Heavy and rough seas are likely to prevail over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and the Bay of Bengal. Fishermen are advised to avoid venturing into the Andaman Sea and along and off Andaman and Nicobar Islands till November 16. Similar advisories have been issued for fishermen in Southeast, Central and Southwest Bay of Bengal.
 Squally weather with wind speeds of 40-50 kmph gusting to 60 kmph is likely till November 16 in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. In the Southwest Bay of Bengal, squally winds of 50-60 kmph gusting to 70 kmph are predicted on November 16. Gale wind speed could reach 60-70 kmph gusting to 80 kmph on November 17.
 Odisha may experience isolated to very heavy rainfall and thundersquall with wind speeds of 50-60 kmph gusting to 70 kmph on November 19-20.
 Arunachal Pradesh, Assam and Meghalaya may experience isolated to scattered rainfall between November 15 and 17. Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram & Tripura could also face isolated to scattered showers from November 16 to 18.
 Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry could face scattered showers till November 20.
 Parts of coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam may face isolated thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds between November and 20.
 A feeble Western Disturbance may affect the Western Himalayan region between November 19 and 25. Some rainfall is likely over Tamil Nadu and Kerala as well during this period. The rainfall will depend upon the track and landfall area of the impending cyclonic storm.
 There are chances of increased rainfall over east and Northeast India around this time.
 Above normal temperatures 
 Above normal weekly minimum temperatures of around 2-4°C are likely over some parts of Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Northwest India, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, east and northeast India.
 The rest of the country will experience near-normal minimum temperatures. There is no probability of a cold wave over any part of the country.
 Delhil will experience a clear sky with mist/shallow fog at most places, with moderate fog at a few places in the morning hours of November 15 to 17.
